meta.description: Deterministic contract corpus for the raw-equality anchor primitive (services/anchors.py). Each case pins how find_all_exact_anchors must behave against a fixed document text. The write gate accepts an anchor ONLY when exactly one span is returned; every other outcome (zero, many, normalization-level miss) is an abstention. This suite proves the deterministic primitive, not any live model.
meta.expected_spans meaning: the list of [start, end) offsets find_all_exact_anchors must return; the gate 'accept' iff its length == 1

cases.note: anchor at the very start of the page
shorter unique substring still resolves to one span

overlapping occurrences are ALL reported (scan advances by 1, not by anchor length): the 20-char anchor recurs at offsets 0, 2, 4... -> many spans -> ambiguous (and >= MIN_ANCHOR_LEN, so it reaches the span check)
an empty anchor raises ValueError -- it must never be treated as a match
raw-unique but under MIN_ANCHOR_LEN=20 -> the patch layer rejects it before the one-span check
exactly 22 chars, raw-unique -> the length gate passes and one span resolves
21 chars raw-unique (guards the MIN_ANCHOR_LEN boundary from the accept side)
a trailing space the source does not have -> not raw-equal
a leading space the source does not have -> not raw-equal
an anchor spanning a paragraph break with the exact newline run is raw-equal and unique
one newline where the source has two -> not raw-equal (whitespace is never folded)
straight ASCII apostrophe matching the source verbatim (unique)
curly apostrophe where the source has a straight one -> not raw-equal (no typography folding)
the entire page text is itself a unique verbatim anchor (upper bound of anchor length within MAX)
